news.title: World Cup 2026 and Cape Verde hero Vozinha snubs Messi's Inter Miami for new club
news.lede: Veteran Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha is set to continue his career in South America after agreeing to join Chilean giants Colo Colo, club president Anibal Mosa confirmed on Friday. The 40-year-old, currently without a club after departing Portuguese second-division outfit Chaves before the FIFA World Cup, is expected to arrive in Chile shortly to complete a medical examination before signing his contract and being presented at the Estadio Monumental. During the World Cup, Vozinha was heavily linked with a move to Inter Miami, which would have allowed him to link up with Messi, with whom he shares a bond. After Cape Verde's thriller against Argentina, Vozinha said that the Argentine maestro praised his work, which was great motivation for him.

news.title: World Cup hero Vozinha has a club but it is not Lionel Messi's Inter Miami
news.lede: After his unexpected yet magnificent World Cup heroics, Cape Verde's star, Vozinha now finally has a club! Josimar José Évora Dias, nicknamed Vozinha, has reached a verbal agreement with Chilean club Colo-Colo. Cape Verde's hero Vozinha to play for Chilean club Colo-ColoCape Verde played their first ever FIFA World Cup in 2026 and instantly became the story of the tournament, thanks to their incredible run. However, their main hero was Vozinha, who made his World Cup debut at 40 and took the football world by storm with his magnificent saves. .

news.title: Arsenal plot return dates for World Cup stars as one trains at former club
news.lede: Arsenal are readying for the return of several of their World Cup stars - but face decisions on how best to manage Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka . Several of the Gunners' players have been back as they're put through their paces, but the majority of their big-hitters were present at this summer's tournament. Those players are entitled to a minimum of three weeks off after their involvement for their countries. England stalwart Rice has been managing neural pain in his hamstring for more than six months.

news.title: Report: Borussia Dortmund makes offer for German ace
news.lede: Borussia Dortmund is taking a swing at FC Köln forward Said El Mala, whose strong Bundesliga campaign last season nearly resulted in a nomination to the German men’s national team for the World Cup. However, the offer — as it stands — is not good enough. Sky Germany’s Patrick Berger has the report: > 🚨⚫️🟡 Exclusive! #BVB has bid for Said El Mala (19/🇩🇪): €26m fixed + €16m in possible bonuses. €8m realistically achievable, the other €8m unrealistic.

news.title: “Messi had already made up his mind”: Leandro Paredes drops a bombshell about the Argentine No. 10's international future
news.lede: Lionel Messi's international future remains one of the biggest questions in world soccer following Argentina's defeat in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, and teammate Leandro Paredes has now suggested that the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner may have already reached a decision. Speaking in an interview shared by Sport Daily on X, the veteran midfielder acknowledged that Messi could have already determined what comes next for his international career, even if the rest of the Argentina squad is hoping he continues wearing the national team's colors. "I think he had already made the decision. I hope that's not the case, and I hope he continues playing, but the decision is his.

news.title: ‘It takes time’ — Dayot Upamecano’s journey to the top
news.lede: Bayern Munich and France men’s national defender Dayot Upamecano is a mainstay these days for club and country — an incredible feat, especially considering the talent available over the years to both sides. But he did not always look like a lock to be a lock in each team’s XI. Bayern fans will recall when Upamecano was the target of criticism following some Champions League exits earlier in his tenure. His time at France was not the smoothest sailing either, in the beginning.

news.title: Missing a major football tournament? Fear not, Wafcon 2026 is about to start
news.lede: The Women’s Africa Cup of Nations starts in Morocco on Sunday, with Cape Verde and Egypt looking to continue feelgood factor from the men’s World Cup and Nigeria going for an 11th title. The men’s World Cup may have finished but do not worry, the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon) is ready to pick up where Spain and Argentina left off. The 34-match event will take place between 26 July and 16 August, which sandwiches it between football’s global showpiece and the start of the league season in Europe. Here’s your guide to one of the most underrated but interesting events on the sporting calendar.
